chunks: Ali (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon the master's death), and he said: 'He is in the position of the will (wasiyyah); the master may revoke him regarding whatever he wishes from it.'

key_terms.اَلْمُدَبَّرُ: A slave manumitted upon the master's death
key_terms.اَلْوَصِيَّةُ: A bequest or will (specifically referring to the portion of estate given to a specific person or entity)
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: He may revoke or return (to the state of slavery)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a Mudabbir slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the juristic classification of the *Mudabbir* (slave manumitted upon the master's death). By equating the *Mudabbir* to a *wasiyyah* (bequest), the Imam establishes that the master retains full discretion to revoke the manumission for any purpose before death, distinguishing it from an immediate, irrevocable free man. This ruling underscores the flexibility of property rights in Shia fiqh, allowing the owner to treat the deferred manumission as a contingent bequest rather than a completed transfer of freedom.
